items.title: Billionaire venture capitalist Vinod Khosla says judge AI by usage, not stock prices
items.summary: Vinod Khosla, the billionaire Sun Microsystems co-founder and early OpenAI backer, says usage is the number to watch, not the stock market's mood swings.

items.title: Are AI Bulls Back? Looks Like It Thanks To Anthropic, CoreWeave, Nvidia
items.summary: AI Bulls are back. AI stocks jumped Wednesday, boosted by CoreWeave results and upbeat feedback from Anthropic’s IPO roadshow.

items.title: Oracle Stocks Climb 7.2% as CoreWeave's Funding Reset Eases AI Debt Fears
items.summary: Oracle now trades above the $116 price of its $10 billion share sale, while new notes carry coupons up to 8.65%.

items.title: Nvidia Vs. AMD: No, Neither is Getting Choked Out By Congress Come January
items.summary: Record AI quarters have NVIDIA and AMD staring down a Congress eager to police where advanced chips can go. One of them already wrote China out of its forecast, and the other still has more to lose than its growth curve suggests.

items.title: Oracle CFO Promises “$30 Billion Plus” in Free Cash Flow by Fiscal 2029 After a 70% Plunge
items.summary: Key TakeawaysOracle CFO Hilary Maxson told CNBC that Oracle will be cash-flow positive in the second half of fiscal 2028 and produce more than $30 billion of free cash flow in fiscal 2029, days after Oracle lost a Tencent deal. Her case rests on capital spending peaking.

items.title: ServiceNow Drops 29% in a Month: Should You Hold or Fold the Stock?
items.summary: NOW shares plunge 29% in a month as slowing backlog growth, rising costs and debt cloud its AI-driven growth prospects. Is it time to hold or fold?

items.title: Oracle CFO: Cloud Demand Strong As Company Touts Growth Targets
items.summary: Oracle Chief Financial Officer Hilary Maxson said the company will add 7 gigawatts of data center capacity.

items.title: Intel’s Turnaround Could Rewrite the Stock’s Story
items.summary: Intel crushed its third quarter, then watched a single guidance call erase a month of gains in one brutal session. Behind the panic sits a server chip bet and a spending cycle that pull in opposite directions.
